audit.why: HARD at 7/10 against 47.94% over 388 games, with a chart of Skill x5 and Karma x2 — a poke lane you lose slightly and win only inside the level 3 to 6 window, which is what the prose says.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 1 section treats Karma as having only a basic Q, and Mantra is never acknowledged as being available before she spends a point on it.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Mantra is available at level 1 and does not require a skill point.' Her very first Inner Flame can be empowered, so the standard 'stand behind the wave and take chip' advice under-rates the level-1 poke. Mantra is 40/38/36/34s and Gathering Fire shortens it every time a damaging ability lands on you, so poking you is how she pays for her next one.
audit.corrected: Added Mantra-at-level-1 to early and the 40s plus Gathering Fire reduction to mid and the cooldown block.
sources: champ-data/_kits/karma.json R description and cooldown, P Gathering Fire

audit.whatIsWrong: The root is attributed to Mantra-Q throughout — 'if she uses RQ right as you drop W, the root+tether from Focused Resolve holds you', 'Mantra-amplified RQ burst', 'her RQ root can interrupt your dive', 'Mantra-empowered RQ tethers and roots you'. Karma's root is on W, not Q, and Mantra-Q has no lockdown whatsoever.
audit.why: Riot text: Focused Resolve (W) — 'creates a tether... If the tether is not broken, the enemy will be rooted... Mantra Bonus: Karma strengthens the link, healing herself and extending the root duration.' Inner Flame (Q) Mantra Bonus — 'creating a cataclysm which deals damage after a short delay.' Damage, no root. A Trundle watching for a root on the wrong ability walks into the real one.
audit.corrected: Every RQ-root reference now names Mantra-empowered Focused Resolve, and Mantra-Q is correctly described as a delayed damage zone.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chomp is credited with an attack-speed debuff in three fields (mid, whys[3], wants.you[0]).
audit.why: Chomp saps Attack Damage and briefly slows. It does not touch attack speed, and against an AP Karma an AD drain is close to irrelevant anyway — the honest reason you win extended trades is Frozen Domain's healing amplification, not a debuff on her.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the AD drain and, where it mattered, with the W healing.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal note despite her Mantra-W healing her through exactly the extended trade the page tells you to force.
audit.why: Focused Resolve's Mantra bonus heals Karma. Since Frozen Domain amplifies healing from all sources for you, Grievous Wounds is a two-way lever in this lane and worth timing.
audit.corrected: Stated the Mantra-W heal in wants.foe[0] and spikes[3] so the anti-heal case is at least visible.

audit.why: Focused Resolve also reveals you (revealsStealth flag, and Riot's text says 'dealing damage and revealing them'), which matters for nothing in this lane — correctly omitted rather than padded in.

edits.before: At Level 1 Karma wins cleanly — her Q deals magic damage from well outside your auto range and you have nothing to close the gap yet. Take Doran's Shield and an MR shard, stand behind the wave to reduce Q angles, and accept minor poke without burning Pillar on a chip shot. Your sustain from King's Tribute on minion deaths keeps you topped up if you don't eat repeated full Q hits. She has no kill pressure solo, so losing a sliver of HP here costs nothing as long as you hit Level 2 without burning Flash. The moment you pick up W at Level 2 the dynamic starts shifting — drop Frozen Domain on yourself whenever she tries to walk up for a Q and she'll have to cast from further away or risk you closing the gap faster than she expects.
edits.after: At Level 1 Karma wins cleanly — Inner Flame deals magic damage from outside your auto range, and Mantra is available at Level 1 without a skill point, so even her first Q can arrive empowered. Take Doran's Shield and an MR shard, stand behind the wave to narrow her Q angles, and never burn Pillar on a chip shot. King's Tribute on minion deaths keeps you topped up if you avoid repeated full Q hits. She has no solo kill pressure, so a sliver of HP costs nothing provided you reach Level 2 with Flash. The moment you pick up W at Level 2 the dynamic shifts — drop Frozen Domain on yourself whenever she walks up for a Q and she has to cast from further out or risk you closing faster than she expects.

edits.before: Level 3 is your first real window: Q, W, and E all online means you can drop Frozen Domain, pop Pillar behind her to cut escape, then run her down with Chomp's AS debuff stacking — she can't kite through your zone and the pillar wall simultaneously. The problem at Levels 4-5 is Mantra cooldown — if she uses RQ right as you drop W, the root+tether from Focused Resolve holds you inside the blast radius, so track her Mantra charges before you engage. Bait the Mantra Q by fake-stepping up without committing W, then when it fires on empty or hits minions, drop Frozen Domain and go. Level 6 is your biggest payoff: Subjugate into any Karma item stack transfers MR directly to you mid-duel, and combined with your W healing she literally cannot output enough damage through your regenerating defences to turn the trade around. Look for Subjugate the instant she's inside Frozen Domain range.
edits.after: Level 3 is your first real window: Q, W, and E all online means you can drop Frozen Domain, pop Pillar behind her to cut escape, then run her down while Chomp drains her AD — she cannot kite through your zone and the pillar wall at once. The problem at Levels 4-5 is Mantra, 40 seconds at rank 1 and shortening every time Gathering Fire triggers off a damaging ability she lands on you. Know which one to fear: the root is Mantra on W, where Focused Resolve heals her and holds you longer, while Mantra on Q is only a delayed cataclysm. Bait it by fake-stepping up without committing W. Level 6 is your payoff: Subjugate into any Karma item stack transfers MR straight to you mid-duel, and with W healing behind you she cannot burn through your defences. Take it the instant she is inside Frozen Domain range.

edits.before: Frozen Domain's movement bonus lets you stick to her through Levels 4-5, and Chomp's AS debuff stacks make extended trades progressively more favourable for you.
edits.after: Frozen Domain's movement bonus lets you stick to her through Levels 4-5, and the healing it amplifies makes every extended trade progressively more favourable for you.

edits.before: Karma's late-game threat is not 1v1 damage — it's the utility she brings in team fights that keeps her out of your reach. Her E shields and hastens an ally while she stays near the back line, and her RQ root can interrupt your dive onto a carry at the worst moment. In a solo lane context you still win the extended duel through 2+ items because Subjugate scales with whatever stats she builds, but in team fights you need to accept that you cannot always reach her if she peels with E on herself. Win the lane in the Level 3-6 window, convert that lead into early objectives and a tower, and let your team composition do the work of forcing her to fight on your terms rather than hers.
edits.after: Karma's late-game threat is not 1v1 damage — it is the utility that keeps her out of your reach. Inspire shields and hastens an ally while she sits at the back, and a Mantra-empowered Focused Resolve root can stop your dive onto a carry at the worst moment. In a solo lane you still win the extended duel through 2+ items, because Subjugate scales with whatever stats she builds, but in team fights accept that you cannot always reach her when she peels with Inspire on herself. Win the lane in the Level 3-6 window, convert that lead into early objectives and a tower, and let your composition force her to fight on your terms rather than hers.

edits.before: You still win the 1v1 duel at 2+ items through Subjugate's scaling, but her RQ root and E peel keep her relevant in team fights even when she can't beat you solo.
edits.after: You still win the 1v1 at 2+ items through Subjugate's scaling, but a Mantra-extended Focused Resolve root and Inspire peel keep her relevant in team fights regardless.

edits.before: Mantra-empowered RQ tethers and roots you inside the wave, letting her kite your W range and string poke together even after your level 6 spike.
edits.after: Mantra on Focused Resolve roots you for longer and heals her through the trade, letting her kite your W range even after your level 6 spike.

edits.before: Reach Karma with Pillar or Frozen Domain active and Chomp an AS-debuffing trade before she can reposition
edits.after: Reach Karma with Pillar or Frozen Domain active and Chomp the AD out of her before she repositions

edits.after: Land Focused Resolve (W), hold the tether to the root, and spend Mantra on it so it lasts longer and heals her

edits.after: - Karma Focused Resolve: matchup-defining — 12s, and Mantra on it extends the root and heals her. Mantra itself is 40s.

notes: Disk 47.94% / 388; packet says 47.94% / 388 too, and also flags the level chart — but the chart here (Skill x5, Karma x2) is fine for a 47.94% lane, so I left it. The RQ-root error was the headline: it appeared in four fields and pointed the reader at the wrong ability entirely. I did not keep the existing claim that the tether 'breaks if you LoS' — Riot's text says only 'if the tether is not broken' and never states the break condition, so asserting line of sight would be a guess.
